rule.description: A host function embeds a duplicate of another function's body instead of delegating to it, while a function still carrying that subordinate responsibility exists in the module. Detected by normalizing every function body into a stream of structural AST tokens (identifiers and literal values erased) and measuring how many of the subordinate's contiguous 8-token windows the host contains; a pair is reported when the subordinate body has at least 40 normalized tokens, the host is at least 3x the subordinate, and window coverage is at least 0.70.

checks.description: Report every host function that carries an inlined copy of a still-existing function's body instead of delegating to it.
checks.detected_relation: host function -> inlined copy of a surviving subordinate function body
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The host mixes higher-level orchestration with the lower-level implementation of a responsibility that already has its own function elsewhere, so the subordinate logic exists twice and the two copies drift independently.

matches.evidence: The per-file zoneErr block inside the reload routine contains the label-map creation and record wiring of Zone.AddLabel (zones/zone.go): lowercase the label name, create the label, spread the record list, register it in the zone.

The zone-options handling inside the reload routine embeds targeting.ParseTargets (targeting/targeting.go): the split-on-space, eight-way case assembly of the targeting bit flags with the unknown-option error.

The reload routine assembles the zone's SOA record inline exactly as Zone.addSOA (zones/zone.go) does: the SOA header from zone parameters, mname/rname/serial/refresh/retry/expire/minttl handling, and registration on the empty-label SOA record list.

The request handler walks the targeting chain itself instead of delegating to Zone.FindLabels (zones/zone.go): resolving each target to a label name, probing the wanted qtype with the MF/CNAME prelude, following MF aliases through the NS/SOA-trimmed type list, and falling back to the empty label match for NOERROR-vs-NXDOMAIN behavior.

The handler assembles the target list itself instead of delegating to TargetOptions.GetTargets (targeting/targeting.go): the bracketed client-IP target, the /24 or /48 masked prefix target, and the global '@' suffix behind its option flag.

The handler picks answer records itself instead of delegating to Zone.Picker (zones/picker.go): the health-filtered copy of the record list, the unweighted pass-through for weight-zero groups, the per-type answer cap with CNAME/MF limited to one, the geo-proximity pass selecting records within 5% of the minimum distance, and the weighted random draw.
Inside its inline picking block the handler re-implements Zone.filterHealth (zones/picker.go): dropping records whose checks report unhealthy and recomputing the weight sum from the survivors.

The handler computes the geographic targets itself instead of delegating to TargetOptions.getGeoTargets (targeting/targeting.go): the ASN lookup against the geo provider, the location lookup with its failed-lookup behavior (nil location, ASN-only targets), the country/continent/region/region-group flags, and the netmask for EDNS scope.

excluded.what: health/healthtest/healthtesters.go tester methods (e.g. the Pingdom and Nodeping Test methods)
excluded.why: Sibling-shaped bodies of comparable size implementing similar protocols; the rule requires the host to be at least 3x the subordinate, so peer-shaped similarity is not a host absorbing a delegated responsibility.

excluded.what: Small answer builders such as the server status/RR and health RR text formatting, and SOA-RR construction inside zones
excluded.why: Shared formatting idioms in small functions; no host/subordinate containment relation under the rule's thresholds.
The rule is applied to production source of the repository module only (non-test .go files of the module under analysis).
